materials.grade-1.entity.title: What is Grade 1 Titanium?
materials.grade-1.entity.description: Grade 1 is the lowest-strength, softest, and most ductile grade in the commercially pure (CP) titanium family. It offers the highest formability and corrosion resistance among CP grades, making it ideal for applications requiring severe forming operations and exposure to corrosive environments.
materials.grade-1.entity.keyCharacterist: Highest formability and ductility among all CP titanium grades
Exceptional corrosion resistance in oxidizing and mildly reducing environments
Low strength compared to alloyed titanium grades
Excellent weldability with minimal post-weld treatment

materials.grade-1.conformsTo.items.2: ASTM B381 — Standard Specification for Titanium and Titanium Alloy Forgings
materials.grade-1.conformsTo.items.3: ASTM B861 — Standard Specification for Titanium and Titanium Alloy Seamless Pipe
materials.grade-1.conformsTo.items.4: ASTM B862 — Standard Specification for Titanium and Titanium Alloy Welded Pipe
materials.grade-1.conformsTo.items.5: AMS 4901 — Sheet, Strip, and Plate (Commercially Pure Titanium)
materials.grade-1.conformsTo.items.6: ISO 5832-2 — Implants for Surgery (Commercially Pure Titanium)

materials.grade-1.processedBy.title: Available Processing Methods
materials.grade-1.processedBy.descriptio: Grade 1 titanium can be processed using the following manufacturing techniques:
materials.grade-1.processedBy.items.0: Cold forming — Excellent; can be severely deformed without intermediate annealing
materials.grade-1.processedBy.items.2: CNC machining — Fair to good; requires sharp tools and slow speeds to prevent work hardening
materials.grade-1.processedBy.items.3: TIG welding — Excellent; no post-weld heat treatment required for most applications
materials.grade-1.processedBy.items.4: Laser welding — Excellent weld quality with proper shielding gas coverage
materials.grade-1.processedBy.items.5: Resistance welding — Suitable for spot and seam welding
materials.grade-1.processedBy.items.6: Chemical etching / pickling — Good response to standard HF/HNO₃ acid baths
materials.grade-1.processedBy.items.7: Electropolishing — Produces bright, clean surface finish
materials.grade-1.processedBy.items.8: Anodizing — Supports Type II and Type III anodizing for enhanced wear and corrosion resistance
materials.grade-1.processedBy.items.9: Hot isostatic pressing (HIP) — Reduces residual porosity in cast or powder forms

materials.grade-2.entity.title: What is Grade 2 Titanium?
materials.grade-2.entity.description: Grade 2 is the most commonly specified commercially pure titanium grade, offering a balanced combination of strength, ductility, corrosion resistance, and weldability. It accounts for the majority of CP titanium usage in industrial applications and is often considered the baseline grade for titanium material selection.
materials.grade-2.entity.keyCharacterist: Most widely used CP titanium grade — industry baseline for many applications
Excellent corrosion resistance in seawater, chlorides, and oxidizing acids
Good balance of strength and formability for fabrication
Excellent weldability — no post-weld heat treatment typically required

materials.grade-3.entity.title: What is Grade 3 Titanium?
materials.grade-3.entity.description: Grade 3 is a medium-strength commercially pure titanium grade positioned between Grade 2 and Grade 4 in the CP family. It offers significantly higher tensile strength than Grade 2 while retaining good ductility and the excellent corrosion resistance characteristic of unalloyed titanium.
materials.grade-3.entity.keyCharacterist: Higher strength than Grade 2 with moderate formability
Excellent corrosion resistance in oxidizing environments
Suitable for moderately loaded structural applications

materials.grade-3.conformsTo.description: Grade 3 titanium conforms to the following international material standards:

materials.grade-4.entity.title: What is Grade 4 Titanium?
materials.grade-4.entity.description: Grade 4 is the highest-strength grade in the commercially pure titanium family. Its elevated oxygen content (up to 0.40%) provides increased tensile and yield strength compared to Grades 1–3, while retaining the excellent corrosion resistance characteristic of unalloyed titanium. Grade 4 is often specified for applications requiring maximum strength within the CP series.
materials.grade-4.entity.keyCharacterist: Highest strength among CP titanium grades
Excellent corrosion resistance in oxidizing and mild reducing environments
Good weldability with appropriate process controls
Moderate formability — less ductile than lower CP grades
Biocompatible — used in medical implant applications

materials.grade-4.processedBy.descriptio: Grade 4 titanium can be processed using the following manufacturing techniques:
materials.grade-4.processedBy.items.0: Cold forming — Limited; higher springback and tooling forces required
materials.grade-4.processedBy.items.1: Hot forming — Recommended for complex geometries; form at 260–540°C (500–1,000°F)

materials.grade-4.processedBy.items.4: Laser welding — Acceptable with proper shielding gas parameters
materials.grade-4.processedBy.items.5: Forging — Open and closed-die forging at 870–980°C (1,600–1,800°F)
materials.grade-4.processedBy.items.6: Extrusion — Hot extrusion at 900–1,050°C with glass lubricants
materials.grade-4.processedBy.items.7: Rolling — Requires intermediate annealing for significant cold reduction
materials.grade-4.processedBy.items.8: Chemical etching — Slower etch rate than lower CP grades

materials.grade-4-eli.entity.title: What is ELI Grade 4 Titanium?
materials.grade-4-eli.entity.description: ELI (Extra-Low Interstitial) Grade 4 is a modified version of standard CP-Ti Grade 4 with strictly controlled lower limits of interstitial elements — oxygen, nitrogen, carbon, and hydrogen. This controlled chemistry significantly improves ductility, fracture toughness, and fatigue properties while maintaining strength levels close to standard Grade 4.
materials.grade-4-eli.entity.classificat: Commercially Pure Titanium (Alpha Phase) — ELI Modification
materials.grade-4-eli.entity.keyCharacte: Superior fracture toughness and fatigue resistance compared to standard Grade 4
Controlled low oxygen (≤0.15%) and nitrogen (≤0.03%) content
Enhanced ductility for improved formability and cold working
Excellent corrosion resistance — equivalent to standard CP grades
Preferred for critical implant applications requiring high reliability

materials.grade-5.entity.title: What is Grade 5 Titanium (Ti-6Al-4V)?
materials.grade-5.entity.description: Grade 5 (Ti-6Al-4V) is the most widely used titanium alloy, accounting for approximately 50% of all titanium consumption globally. It is an alpha-beta alloy containing 6% aluminum (alpha stabilizer) and 4% vanadium (beta stabilizer), providing an excellent balance of strength, ductility, fracture toughness, and corrosion resistance at temperatures up to 400°C (750°F).
materials.grade-5.entity.keyCharacterist: Best combination of strength, weight, and corrosion resistance among titanium alloys
Heat treatable — strength can be tailored via solution treatment and aging
Excellent fatigue properties for cyclic loading applications
Good weldability with proper filler metal and shielding
Service temperature up to 400°C (750°F) in oxidizing environments
Industry standard for aerospace structural components

materials.grade-23.entity.title: What is Grade 23 Titanium (Ti-6Al-4V ELI)?
materials.grade-23.entity.description: Grade 23 (Ti-6Al-4V ELI, Extra Low Interstitial) is a modified version of Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V with reduced oxygen content (maximum 0.13% vs 0.20% in Grade 5) and tighter control of nitrogen, carbon, and hydrogen. This ELI chemistry significantly improves ductility, fracture toughness, and fatigue performance, making it the preferred material for implantable medical devices and cryogenic applications requiring superior reliability.
materials.grade-23.entity.keyCharacteris: Superior fracture toughness (KIC) compared to standard Grade 5
Enhanced ductility and fatigue resistance for long-term implant reliability
Reduced notch sensitivity for improved performance in threaded implant designs
Cryogenic-grade toughness — suitable for LNG and liquid hydrogen service
Corrosion resistance equivalent to standard Ti-6Al-4V

materials.grade-23.processedBy.items.8: Surface treatment — Passivation, anodizing, plasma spraying for osseointegration

materials.grade-6.entity.title: What is Grade 6 Titanium (Ti-5Al-2.5Sn)?
materials.grade-6.entity.description: Grade 6 (Ti-5Al-2.5Sn) is a near-alpha titanium alloy stabilized with 5% aluminum and 2.5% tin. It offers an excellent combination of medium strength, oxidation resistance, and creep strength at elevated temperatures up to 480°C (900°F). Its alpha-phase microstructure provides superior weldability and thermal stability compared to alpha-beta alloys.

Good oxidation resistance for continuous high-temperature service
Superior weldability compared to alpha-beta alloys

Excellent thermal stability — no significant embrittlement after prolonged thermal exposure
Good corrosion resistance in oxidizing environments

materials.grade-9.entity.title: What is Grade 9 Titanium (Ti-3Al-2.5V)?
materials.grade-9.entity.description: Grade 9 (Ti-3Al-2.5V) is a medium-strength alpha-beta titanium alloy that provides a balance of strength and formability superior to CP titanium grades while being more readily formable than Grade 5 (Ti-6Al-4V). It is particularly valued for its excellent cold formability, making it the standard material for aerospace hydraulic and pneumatic tubing systems.

Good strength-to-weight ratio between CP grades and Ti-6Al-4V
Outstanding corrosion resistance — equivalent to CP titanium
Good weldability with proper process controls
Preferred material for thin-wall seamless tubing
Excellent fatigue strength in tubular form

materials.grade-19.entity.title: What is Grade 19 Titanium (Ti-10V-2Fe-3Al)?
materials.grade-19.entity.description: Grade 19 (Ti-10V-2Fe-3Al) is a beta-rich titanium alloy developed specifically for high-strength forged components. Its deep hardenability allows uniform mechanical properties through thick sections — a critical advantage over alpha-beta alloys that exhibit property gradients in heavy cross-sections. It achieves tensile strengths up to 1,240 MPa (180 ksi) with good fracture toughness.
materials.grade-19.entity.keyCharacteris: Very high strength — up to 1,240 MPa (180 ksi) achievable
Deep hardenability — uniform properties through thick sections
Excellent forgeability in the beta phase field
Good fracture toughness at high strength levels

Heat treatable with solution treatment and aging

materials.grade-21.entity.title: What is Grade 21 Titanium (Ti-15V-3Cr-3Sn-3Al)?
materials.grade-21.entity.description: Grade 21 (Ti-15V-3Cr-3Sn-3Al, also known as Ti-15-3) is a metastable beta titanium alloy developed for applications requiring a combination of exceptional room-temperature formability and very high post-aging strength. In the solution-treated condition, it can be cold formed similarly to CP titanium, then aged to achieve tensile strengths exceeding 1,170 MPa (170 ksi).

materials.grade-6242.entity.title: What is Grade 6242 Titanium (Ti-6Al-2Sn-4Zr-2Mo)?
materials.grade-6242.entity.description: Grade 6242 (Ti-6Al-2Sn-4Zr-2Mo) is a near-alpha titanium alloy designed for high-temperature service in gas turbine engines and advanced airframes. It combines alpha-phase strength and creep resistance from aluminum and tin with solid-solution strengthening from zirconium and molybdenum. It is capable of continuous service at temperatures up to 540°C (1,000°F), significantly higher than Ti-6Al-4V.

Weldable with proper process controls and post-weld heat treatment
Commonly used in the silicide-bearing variant (Ti-6242S) with 0.1% Si

materials.ti-5553.entity.title: What is Ti-5Al-5V-5Mo-3Cr (Ti-5553)?
materials.ti-5553.entity.description: Ti-5Al-5V-5Mo-3Cr (commonly known as Ti-5553) is a metastable beta titanium alloy developed as a successor to Ti-10V-2Fe-3Al (Grade 19). It offers superior deep-section hardenability — enabling uniform mechanical properties in cross-sections up to 150 mm (6 inches) — combined with an excellent balance of high strength, fracture toughness, and fatigue resistance.

Superior fatigue crack growth resistance compared to Ti-6Al-4V
Good forgeability with wide processing window

Increasingly preferred for next-generation landing gear and airframe structures
